newsitem.title: CHINA: China makes low-key approach to Taiwan-U.S. meeting.
newsitem.headline: China makes low-key approach to Taiwan-U.S. meeting.

text.p: China on Tuesday made a low-key response to a meeting between a senior U.S. official and the president of rival Taiwan.
U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers met President Lee Teng-hui on Tuesday in the most senior U.S.-Taiwan contact in nearly two years.

Beijing had earlier signalled it would be displeased by Summer's visit, but at a regular Foreign Ministry news briefing spokesman Shen Guofang took a relatively mild approach, saying Washington had promised to stick to its "One China" principles.
"The U.S. side has said it will abide by the promises it has made ...and that it would handle the Taiwan problem on the basis of the 'One China' stance," Shen said.
"I hope the U.S. side will keep on alert and not do anything to hurt the progress of Sino-U.S. relations again," he said.

The Lee-Summers talks came more than a year after Taiwan's president visited the United States in a trip that chilled Sino-U.S. ties. Washington recognises Beijing but maintains unofficial relations with Taipei.
Beijing opposes all attempts by Taiwan, its rival since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, to break out of its diplomatic isolation.
Taiwan is recognised by only 30 countries but uses its economic strength to keep close business ties with many of China's diplomatic partners.
Asked about recent visits by Taiwan leaders abroad, Shen said other countries should be wary of Taipei's motives and accused Taiwan of secretly trying to split China.
"The Taiwan authorities do not sincerely want to improve relations and reunite the nation peacefully," Shen said.
"Taiwan has continually used all kinds of methods ...to promote its so-called 'pragmatic diplomacy'," he said. "Its goal is to split the motherland."
Chinese state media on Tuesday accused Taiwan of using cash payments to gain support from other countries for its bid to rejoin the United Nations.
